meta.purpose: Feasibility register for expanding the guide beyond Tarrant, Dallas and Collin. One row per county: can it be done, from what source, and what has to be derived.
meta.scope: Top 25 Texas counties by registered voters. Not loaded by the site; reference data for the ingestion work.
meta.verification: Every url marked VERIFIED was fetched live as ArcGIS service JSON and its field list read from the response. UNVERIFIED means the endpoint could not be reached. No url in this file was guessed.
caveats: registeredVoters figures are PROVISIONAL. They were extracted from the Texas SOS March 2026 registration page and the extraction returned internally inconsistent ranks (e.g. Tarrant listed below Bexar despite a higher count, El Paso implausibly low). Treat the SET of counties as sound and the NUMBERS as needing a second pass against the SOS source before anyone relies on them.
districtFieldsPresent describes what the precinct layer itself carries. Most counties carry almost nothing, which is the central finding of this register.

headlineFindings: Only 5 of 25 counties ship a usable set of district attributes on the precinct polygon (Travis, Denton-2024, Montgomery, Fort Bend, Brazoria). Lubbock and McLennan ship a partial set. The rest carry a precinct id and nothing else.
This is a design consequence, not a data-entry one: the ingestion pipeline needs a point-in-polygon spatial join against separate district layers as a first-class capability, not a special case.

HARRIS IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. Its layer returns a populated district value for every precinct, so nothing errors, but the boundaries are pre-2021-redistricting (effective 2016, field names encode old plan ids). It would silently place voters in the wrong congressional and legislative races. Do not ship Harris off this layer.

EL PASO IS THE SAME TRAP IN REVERSE. REPDIST / STATEDIST / CONGRESSDI exist in the schema but are 100% NULL across all 221 rows. A naive field-mapping script would map them and produce empty districts.
BELL: DISTRICT_1 and DISTRICT_2 are row-sequence artifacts, not district identifiers. Do not map them.

CONFLICT, UNRESOLVED: the TLC statewide layer at services6.arcgis.com/bRCQlwH4ROCI4sNr/.../Voting_Precincts/FeatureServer/0 is described as a statewide 2022 precinct file and three researchers recommended it as a fallback. A fourth actually queried it and got 16 features, all CNTY=99 (Hardeman). It is either a fragment published under a statewide description or the query was wrong. Resolve before relying on it. It surfaces at the top of search for nearly every county, so it will keep coming up.

counties.name: Harris
counties.notes: Effective 2016. Pre-2021 redistricting. Districts populated but WRONG for 2026. Old-style MapServer: Shape.STArea() with parentheses breaks naive outField handling. Need current boundaries from Harris County Elections or TLC.

counties.name: Dallas
counties.notes: Already live on the site. FIRST_DIST* fields were renamed to match Tarrant's schema during ingestion.

counties.name: Tarrant
counties.notes: Already live on the site. Used as published; this is the schema the other counties are normalized onto.

counties.name: Bexar
counties.notes: Current and authoritative but deliberately thin. Bexar publishes each district type as its own service on the same host: USCongressDistricts, TXHouseRepDistricts, TXSenateDistrictsBexar, TX_SBOE_Districts, CommissionerPrecincts, JusticeofthePeace. A flattened copy with districts exists at services3.arcgis.com/9PNlWtkdnlKGwbiK/... but is owned by a PERSONAL account, not the county. Given this project cites public records, do not source districts from it.

counties.name: Travis
counties.notes: Complete district set, no join needed. Field names truncated to 10 chars from a shapefile round-trip - use those exact spellings. Hosted by CITY OF AUSTIN, not the county; confirm currency via CREATED/LASTEDITED. Same service carries Williamson at layer 1 and Hays at layer 2, plus statewide Senate/House/Congressional at 3/4/5.

counties.name: Collin
counties.notes: Already live on the site. District fields renamed to match Tarrant's during ingestion.

counties.name: Denton
counties.notes: Two layers, need both. Current geometry (2026) has commissioner only. The 2024 layer has the full district set but stale geometry. Join current->2024 on old_VP -> PRECINCT_N; that is what old_VP exists for. New or split precincts will have no match and need a spatial fallback. Alternate layer sits at id 138, not 0, and its service description wrongly says 'The Colony'.

counties.name: Fort Bend
counties.notes: No JP field. Named 2022 but AGOL item modified Oct 2025. County ran a 'FBC Voter Precincts Updates 2025' web map, so boundaries may have shifted - verify vintage. FED_CONGRE is a double where others are strings.

counties.name: Montgomery
counties.notes: Richest schema found. All six district types on the polygon. TRAP: searching surfaces opendata-mcgov-gis.hub.arcgis.com which is Montgomery County MARYLAND. Texas is gis.mctx.org.

counties.name: Williamson
counties.notes: OID field is OBJECTID_1, not OBJECTID. Shape fields are uppercase SHAPE__Area where others use Shape__Area - case matters. Travis's City-of-Austin service also carries Williamson precincts at layer 1, worth comparing.

counties.name: Hidalgo
counties.notes: Zero-padding differs between fields: PCT_NUM='001' but DISTRICT='1'. Congressional/state/SBOE are separate services in the same org: State_House_of_Representatives, State_Senate, State_Board_of_Education, PLANC2333. Org is run by the elections dept, not a formal open-data portal, so service names may change without notice.

counties.name: Brazoria
counties.notes: Complete district set. CCJPCOM appears to serve as both commissioner and JP - verify against the certified ballot whether Brazoria's JP precincts equal commissioner precincts. Numeric fields return as floats, cast to int. MapServer: pagination NOT supported, resultRecordCount returns HTTP 400. Pull all 84 at once.

counties.name: Galveston
counties.notes: No district fields at all. WATCH: Galveston's precinct map has been in litigation - the Texas Supreme Court ruled the county could not use a new precinct map in November. Verify this layer's vintage against the certified SOS ballot before shipping.

counties.name: Cameron
counties.notes: County ownership confirmed by the Contact field on every feature (isaac.gallegos@co.cameron.tx.us). No district fields. Queries hit exceededTransferLimit at default page size - paginate. Same org has 2022_Commissioners and 2022_Justice_of_the_Peace_Constable layers to fill the gaps. The county's own Hub site does NOT publish precincts; the layer is only reachable via the Experience app's web map.

counties.name: Bell
counties.notes: DISTRICT_1 and DISTRICT_2 are NOT districts - they are row sequence artifacts (1..8 in row order). Do not map them. Three conflicting vintages in one dataset: item titled 2026, path says 2022, layer name says June 2025. Owner is a personal-looking AGOL account, not a branded county account. Confirm with Bell County Elections. An older sibling (Voting_Precincts, 49 features) is the only Bell source carrying a commissioner attribute (COMMISSION) - stale geometry but usable as a crosswalk.

counties.name: Nueces
counties.notes: Owner is Nueces County Public Works, but the service is named like an in-progress redistricting comparison map, not a published product. Three near-identical siblings exist; the un-numbered one has the richest schema. County has no open-data hub and its Election GIS page is marked 'under construction'. Weakest governance of the set - re-verify each cycle.

counties.name: Lubbock
counties.notes: Populated and current (last edited Aug 2026). Also carries City, CityCouncil, SchoolDistrict - useful for the local races that are this project's differentiator. Congressional/senate/SBOE are separate layers in the SAME service: 15 USCongressRepresentative, 13 Senate Representative, 16 StateHouseRepresentative, 17 StateBoardofEducation. It is an editing dataset, so schema could shift.

counties.name: Hays
counties.notes: Hays redrew precincts effective Jan 1 2026 and this layer reflects it. Leading digit of VTD encodes commissioner precinct 1-4. The companion district service publishes TX Senate, TX House, JP and commissioner as POLYLINE layers only - you cannot point-in-polygon against lines, so those need another source.

counties.name: El Paso
counties.notes: REPDIST / STATEDIST / CONGRESSDI exist but are 100% NULL across all 221 rows. The schema looks mappable and is not. Hosted by CITY of El Paso, but extent confirmed countywide (reaches ~13mi past city limits into Fabens/Tornillo). TRAP: opendata-elpasoco.hub.arcgis.com and gisservices.elpasoco.com are El Paso County COLORADO.

counties.name: Jefferson
counties.notes: Raw export of a redistricting tool, hence the Population/Locked/Compactnes cruft. No district fields. A PROPOSED Oct 2025 redraw exists in the same org - do not ship it, but Jefferson appears to be mid-redistricting so the 121-precinct layer may be superseded. Sibling Precinct_Boundaries/0 is actually 2018 commissioner precincts.

counties.name: Comal
counties.notes: Leanest schema found. County-hosted ArcGIS Server, so geometry fields use the Shape.STArea() spelling - quote carefully in outFields. Whole DataPortal folder enumerated; CommissionerPrecinctsOpenData is the only other election service, so no richer Comal layer exists.

counties.name: McLennan
counties.notes: Hosted by City of Waco GIS, modified Oct 2025. Also carries RegVoters/UN_RegVot counts, unusual and useful. AVOID services.arcgis.com/VcImACesgvxI5yNd/.../McLennanCountyVotingPcts - same feature count but last modified May 2017. Equivalent fresh second source: gis.wacotx.gov/server/rest/services/PublicMap/PublicMap_Boundary/FeatureServer/6.

counties.name: Smith
counties.notes: Clean and current, no district attributes. COUNTY field is null on every feature - do not use it to confirm you are in Smith County, confirm by extent. Published by the Smith County 911 District, which is the authoritative address/boundary maintainer there.

counties.name: Brazos
counties.notes: Published by the county itself, most recent of several vintages (2024, 2022, 2021 siblings exist for reconciliation). TRAPS: Brazos_County_GOP_Precincts at services3/hdqlzaa4UWs4xwZ1 looks perfect in search but returns error 499 Token Required - not public. A widely-linked Hub dataset titled 'Voting Precincts' (e1d44334...) is Jackson County OREGON.

counties.name: Guadalupe
counties.notes: URL is genuine - it is the url field of the county's own AGOL item, linked from the official open-data hub. But every live fetch failed: ?f=pjson read-timed-out and /query returned HTTP 503. The whole county ArcGIS Server appears down or geo-blocked, not just this layer. Field list and count above come from ArcGIS Hub CACHED metadata - probable, not confirmed. RETRY before building. Fallback: Hub shapefile export at open-data-guadalupetx.hub.arcgis.com/api/download/v1/items/35facd463e9842a4abfb67b722918c39/shapefile?layers=0 (served by Esri, not the county host). Do NOT substitute services.arcgis.com/nm045BuyQhRAuLir/.../Precincts_new - that is 4 features, i.e. commissioner precincts.

techniques: arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=... returns an empty SPA shell and is useless to a fetcher. Use https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/{id}?f=pjson to get an item's real service url.

https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search?q=owner:{org}&f=pjson enumerates a county org's services. This is what actually located most of these layers - several counties do not link their precinct layer from any public page.
Direct curl to arcgis.com and county GIS hosts is blocked by the agent proxy (403 on CONNECT). Verification has to go through a fetcher that follows the proxy.
Always include 'Texas' in searches. Montgomery, Jefferson, Smith, Brazos and El Paso all have same-named counties in other states that outrank the Texas one in search results.
